An oil tank is leaking q(t) liters of oil after t hours. The graph of q(t) is shown above.

Approximate the rate at which the oil is leaking from the tank when t=2 using a central difference approximation with step size h=1.

a
0.5liters/hour
b
1liter/hour
c
2.5liters/hour
d
1.5liters/hour
e
2liters/hour

decision.explanation: The central difference gives q'(2) ≈ [q(3)−q(1)]/(2h). From the graph, q(3) ≈ 3 and q(1) ≈ 2, so q'(2) ≈ (3−2)/2 = 0.5 liters/hour.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069816/assets/fa3045b53d5a91ae7adbf450243338b988239749e4ae7340938943cce4c239fb.png)

An oil tank is leaking $q(t)$ liters of oil after $t$ hours.
 The graph of $q(t)$ is shown above.

Approximate the rate at which the oil is leaking from the tank when $t=2$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
after.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{q}^{′}(t)≈\frac{q(t+h)-q(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=2$ and step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}^{′}(2) & ≈\frac{q(2+1)-q(2-1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{q(3)-q(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3-2}{2} \\  & =0.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of leaking at the instant of time $t=2$ is $0.5\,\text{liters}/\text{hour}.$

Question 1

An oil tank is leaking q(t) liters of oil after t hours. The graph of q(t) is shown above.

Approximate the rate at which the oil is leaking from the tank when t=2 using a central difference approximation with step size h=1.

a
0.5liters/hour
b
1liter/hour
c
2.5liters/hour
d
1.5liters/hour
e
2liters/hour
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We use the central difference approximation q′(t)≈q(t+h)−q(t−h)2h, at the time t=2 and step size h=1. This gives

q′(2)≈q(2+1)−q(2−1)2=q(3)−q(1)2=3−22=0.5.

Therefore, the rate of leaking at the instant of time t=2 is 0.5liters/hour.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14069816/assets/1e11260301be8c0bb19a9fd47ffbbf71cc5fa4d94dbeae57af934b76fb17f0e1.png)

A particle has a speed of $v(t)$ meters per second after $t$ seconds. The graph of $v(t)$ is shown above. Approximate the rate of change of speed when $t=3$ using a central difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
after.worked_solution:
We use the central difference approximation

$$
{v}^{′}(x)≈\frac{v(t+h)-g(t-h)}{2h},
$$

 
at the time $t=2$ and step size $h=1.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{′}(2) & ≈\frac{v(3+1)-v(3-1)}{2(1)} \\  & =\frac{v(4)-v(2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{3-1}{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of speed at the instant of time $t=2$ is approximately $1\,\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2}.$
